title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Anna Patel
content:
Summary:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for: access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and internal templates. It is intended as the single reference for employees and managers to understand rules, approval flows, and where to find supporting templates and forms.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Provide clear, centralized policies that reduce risk, enable scalable operations, and streamline approvals across the company.
- Scope: All Redwood employees, contractors, and vendors who interact with Redwood systems, data, finances, or travel booking processes.

1) Access & permissions
Purpose: Ensure least-privilege access, secure onboarding/offboarding, and consistent ownership of access reviews.
Policy statements:
- Principle of least privilege: Accounts and roles should grant the minimum permissions required for an individual to perform their job.
- RBAC is primary: Use platform RBAC (Okta groups + internal role mapping) rather than individual policies where possible.
- Time-limited access: Temporary elevated access must be requested via the access request form and expires automatically after the approved window.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Manager: approves access requests for team members; confirms access on quarterly reviews.
- Security team: maintains baseline role definitions, performs quarterly access audits, and approves exceptions.
- IT / SRE: implements access changes in cloud accounts and infra tools within SLA.

Standard procedures (onboarding, change, offboarding):
1. Onboarding:
   a. Manager opens a new-hire request in HRIS (Greenhouse/Workday) and selects job role.
   b. HR system triggers account provisioning workflow in Okta and Slack.
   c. New hires are automatically assigned baseline groups: all-staff, engineering-orientation (if applicable), and office access.
2. Requesting elevated access:
   1) Submit Access Request form (link in Templates). Include justification, duration, and owner.
   2) Manager approval required.
   3) Security performs risk check for sensitive resources (prod, KMS, PII).
   4) Changes implemented by IT within 8 business hours for standard requests; emergency requests handled per Incident process.
3. Offboarding:
   - HR signals offboard in HRIS; Okta deprovisions accounts within 1 business hour for terminated users, 24 hours for standard departures.
   - Managers must return company assets and confirm access removal on exit checklist.

Access reviews and SLOs:
- Quarterly access review: managers confirm team memberships and role assignments.
- Sensitive access review: monthly review for prod, KMS, and audit-log viewers.
- Target SLA for provisioning: 90% of standard access requests completed within 8 hours.

2) Change management
Purpose: Reduce production risk by standardizing how changes to infrastructure, runtime, and customer-facing systems are planned, reviewed and executed.
Policy statements:
- All changes that affect production must be tracked in the Change Log and follow the change classification (Standard, Minor, Major, Emergency).
- No direct changes to production outside an approved change window unless declared Emergency and runbook invoked.

Change classification and approvals:
- Standard Change: low-risk, pre-approved (e.g., certificate rotations, scheduled DB maintenance). Requires change request with automated approval.
- Minor Change: routine config or non-customer-impacting deploys. Requires owner + peer reviewer.
- Major Change: architecture or capacity changes, schema migrations, model rollouts with customer impact potential. Requires owner, engineering manager, product ORS, and SRE approval.
- Emergency Change: must follow Incident Response steps and be documented post-facto in the Change Log.

Change process (numbered steps):
1) Create a Change Request in the change management tool (link in Templates). Include RFC, rollback plan, test plan, and deploy window.
2) Assign reviewers: SRE for infra, Security for access/secret handling, Product for customer impact.
3) Execute in a controlled window; record start/end times and runbook steps.
4) Post-change verification: owner completes verification checklist within 2 hours and updates the change record.
5) Postmortem for Major/Emergency changes within 7 days.

Change windows and blackout periods:
- Standard deploy window: Mon-Fri 02:00-05:00 PT for non-urgent infra changes.
- Blackout: Major public launches or fiscal close - no Major changes during blackout without executive approval.

3) Data management
Purpose: Classify, handle, and retain data safely to meet compliance and operational needs.
Data classification levels:
- Public: Documentation intended for public consumption. No restrictions.
- Internal: Company-internal operational data (most Confluence docs, internal dashboards).
- Confidential: Customer metadata, contracts, internal roadmaps. Access limited to business need.
- Restricted/PII: Customer data that includes personal identifiers, payment information, or regulated data. Strict controls, encryption at rest + transit, and limited audit logging.

Policy highlights:
- Encryption: All Restricted/PII and Confidential data must be encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS1.2+).
- Data minimization: Services should only persist fields required for the product.
- Retention: Default retention for logs = 90 days (hot), 2 years (cold) unless business reason requires longer and is approved by Legal.
- Anonymization: Use irreversible hashing or tokenization for datasets used in analysis when possible.

Data access & sharing:
- Access requests for Confidential/Restricted data require business justification and approval from data owner + Security.
- Third-party data transfers require a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) and Legal approval.

Backups & disaster recovery:
- Critical databases: RPO <= 1 hour, RTO <= 4 hours.
- Backups tested quarterly and restore exercises documented in the DR Runbook.

4) Procurement & expenses
Purpose: Provide a transparent, auditable process for spending company funds and engaging vendors.
Policy thresholds and approval matrix:
- < $1,000: Manager approval. Can be submitted via expense report.
- $1,000-$25,000: Department head approval + procurement notification.
- > $25,000: Procurement + Finance + VP approval; legal review for contracts.
- Capital equipment (> $5,000 per unit): tag as capex and route through Finance.

Procurement process (numbered):
1) Complete Purchase Request form (template). Include vendor, SKU/description, business justification, cost center, and preferred vendor.
2) Procurement team obtains at least two competitive quotes for purchases > $5,000.
3) Finance confirms budget; Legal reviews contracts for term > 12 months or payments > $25,000.
4) PO issued and purchase tracked in ERP.

Expenses & travel reimbursements:
- Employees should submit expenses within 30 days of occurrence with receipts.
- Per diem allowances (see Travel section).
- Card usage: corporate cards must be used for approved vendor subscriptions; personal cards are allowed when pre-approved and reimbursed with receipts.

5) Vendor management
Purpose: Standardize onboarding, security, and lifecycle management of third-party vendors and SaaS providers.
Vendor onboarding checklist:
- Business owner nominates vendor and completes Vendor Intake form (see Templates).
- Procurement validates vendor setup, payment terms, and SOW.
- Security performs a security review for vendors with access to systems/data; high-risk vendors require SOC 2 Type II or equivalent and a penetration test report.
- Legal executes contract and DPA where applicable.

Vendor risk categories and controls:
- Low risk: Public content or non-sensitive SaaS (e.g., marketing tools). Standard onboarding.
- Medium risk: Tools with limited access to internal systems (e.g., analytics dashboards). Require security questionnaire.
- High risk: Vendors with production access, PII, or system-level privileges. Require SOC 2, DPA, and periodic audits.

Ongoing vendor governance:
- Annual vendor review for high/medium risk vendors: business owner + procurement + security.
- Maintain an approved-vendors registry with contract expiry reminders.

6) Travel policy (business travel and expenses)
Purpose: Enable safe, cost-effective business travel while providing reasonable employee comfort and compliance with local laws.
Booking and approvals:
- All travel > $500 estimated requires manager pre-approval. International travel requires travel advisory check and E&S review (if customer-sensitive).
- Employees must use the company travel portal for flights and hotels when possible to ensure negotiated rates and insurance coverage.

Allowances and expense categories:
- Flights: Economy for < 6 hours; Premium Economy or Comfort for flights between 6-10 hours; Manager discretion for > 10 hours with VP approval.
- Hotels: Standard business hotels; a mid-range option is preferred for multi-night stays.
- Meals: Per diem or actuals with receipts; alcohol limited to client entertainment with approval.
- Ground transport: Use ride-share or rental car with reasonable class; receipts required.

Health & safety:
- Company has travel insurance for employees traveling on company business. Register international trips with People Ops.

Travel expense submission:
1) Submit trip claim within 30 days with itemized receipts and business purpose.
2) Manager approves; Finance processes reimbursement within 10 business days.

7) Internal templates and links
This section lists common templates and where to find them in the Templates library (Confluence).
- Access Request form (link): temporary access requests, includes fields for justification and expiry date.
- Change Request / RFC template: required fields, rollback plan, test plan, and approvers.
- Purchase Request and Vendor Intake forms: procurement initiation and vendor onboarding.
- Travel expense template: per diem and receipts checklist.
- Offboarding checklist: asset return, access revocation steps, and exit interview.

Governance, exceptions, and escalation
- Exceptions: Any deviations from policy must be documented and approved by the policy owner and Security/Finance as appropriate. Exceptions are temporary and logged in the Exceptions register.
- Escalation: Policy disputes escalate to the policy owner (People Ops) then to the Head of People Ops; operational disputes may escalate to the relevant functional VP.

Training & awareness
- Annual mandatory policy review: all employees must complete the company policies training module yearly.
- Role-based training: security and procurement workshops for engineers and managers as scheduled.

Appendix: quick reference tables
1) Procurement approval matrix:
| Amount | Approver(s) | Notes |
| < $1,000 | Manager | Expense report accepted |
| $1,000-$25,000 | Dept Head + Procurement | Two quotes for > $5k |
| > $25,000 | Procurement + Finance + VP | Legal review required |

2) Data classification summary:
| Classification | Examples | Controls |
| Public | Marketing site, blog | No special controls |
| Internal | Internal docs, dashboards | Confluence access; internal-only |
| Confidential | Contracts, product roadmaps | RBAC, limited groups |
| Restricted/PII | Customer PII, payment data | Encryption, DPA, audit logs |

Contact and ownership
- Policy owner: People Ops (policies@redwood-inference.com).
- Security contact: security@redwood-inference.com.
- Procurement: procurement@redwood-inference.com.
- Finance: expenses@redwood-inference.com.

- 2026-02-15: Added encryption and backup SLAs; clarified access provisioning SLAs.
